headline: Preferred energy pick, benefiting from high oil prices and elevated refining margins offering stability and upside in uncertain conditions

headline: Another RBA rate hike expected at the 29 September meeting, with oil prices, the Strait of Hormuz uncertainty and a tight labour market all keeping pressure on
reasoning: David Lane noted that most economists are predicting another rate rise in Australia, consistent with signals from RBA Governor Michelle Bullock. He highlighted elevated oil prices, ongoing uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz, a strong employment market, and sticky inflation as the key drivers keeping the RBA in a difficult position. He also observed that despite ~$40 billion in dividends hitting bank accounts in September and another $10 billion in October, investors are largely sitting on the sidelines or rotating into more defensive positions.
quote: She's thrown out the narrow path discussion and is now talking about, yeah, the very real prospect of a rate rise without saying that. But definitely the Reserve Bank and many others are concerned about the global issues that we're facing and the fact that the oil price remains very, very high. There is continued uncertainty as far as the Strait of Hormuz is concerned. And then the fact that in Australia we're still battling with a very strong employment market and prices aren't coming down. So, yeah, the Reserve Bank is still very much caught there.

headline: Banks sold off on rate rises and budget changes but value is starting to emerge, with bargain hunters beginning to return
reasoning: David Lane noted that Australian banks have sold off significantly due to rising interest rates and budget changes, and all banks have reported a reduction in mortgage applications and investor appetite. However, he believes the market has adjusted to these headwinds and value is beginning to appear in the sector, with investors starting to provide more support to bank stocks.
quote: We've seen the banks sell off fairly significantly, obviously, with the increase in the rates as well as the changes to the budget. All of the banks have told us that they're seeing a reduction in mortgage applications and investor appetites. So I think the market's adjusted to that. And we are starting to see a little bit more value coming into those stocks. So investors are starting to give a little bit more support to some of those banks.
